signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Blockade + G10 Laggard
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 159.42, holding just below the SMA20/50 cluster at 160.93/161.15. The Strait of Hormuz remains blocked with no clear timeline for reopening, a TIER-1 geopolitical shock that typically supports JPY safe-haven demand, yet the currency remains the G10 laggard with a -0.763% weekly average performance. A 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry differential continues to anchor the pair's bid, while the options market reflects growing anxiety via a strong -2.16 25d risk reversal. This creates a sharp divergence: the 275bp carry advantage favors the USD, but a -1.5% VRP and the blocked waterway suggest the JPY is under-priced for a volatility spike. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance persists while VIX remains below 25. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 48% hike priced) — hike bias active. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a disorderly unwind of the -63,633 COT spec short position.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Support
signals.text: CAD/JPY represents the extreme G10 bilateral theme as CAD outperforms (avg +0.723%) while JPY lags (avg -0.763%), creating a 1.485% spread. This strength in the Loonie aligns with a positive ESI of +12.0 and restrictive real policy rates of +0.15%, contrasting with JPY's accommodative -0.70% real rate. Despite the Strait of Hormuz blockade, JPY weakness persists as the carry-funding currency of choice, providing a 125bp OIS carry advantage to CAD. The pair benefits from CAD's resilience in a 'bull steepener' yield curve regime where growth-linked currencies with positive data surprises find buyers. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY; divergence between top and bottom G10 performers remains intact. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: JPY safe-haven bid finally engages on sustained energy supply fears, compressing the 1.485% spread.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5861, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5846/0.5788/0.5831). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This negative positioning against a hawkish central bank creates an asymmetric short-squeeze risk if upcoming inflation expectations data surprises to the upside. While the Fed-RBNZ OIS spread of +125bp favors the USD, the crowded spec short in NZD lacks a fundamental catalyst for further expansion given the RBNZ's outlier status as the only G10 bank actively hiking. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze potential against crowded speculative shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ inflation expectations release 13 Aug. Risk: NZD inflation data misses significantly, validating the record spec short and breaking the SMA200 support.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3493 is testing the upper bounds of its SMA20/50/200 cluster, all of which reside between 1.3368 and 1.3425. The options market is pricing a significant risk premium with 1M IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 6.0%, a +5.0% VRP that reflects aggressive hedging for Sterling downside. This hedging occurs despite a neutral 0bp OIS carry differential and a restrictive GBP real rate of +0.93% which supports the currency fundamentally. Speculative positioning remains net long (+39,039), but the high vol premium suggests institutional desks are paying up for protection rather than adding to spot exposure at these levels. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium suggests range-bound price action despite bullish technicals. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) — market bias Hold. Risk: Sharp compression in the VRP alongside a break of 1.3500 re-engages trend followers.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Extreme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: USD/NOK is currently at 9.487, trading well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (9.578-9.699). Retail sentiment has reached a 100% long extreme, an absolute contrarian signal that typically precedes further downside when institutional flows are absent. This retail positioning fades the Norges Bank's restrictive +1.51% real rate, which is currently the highest in the G10 alongside the USD. With WTI oil at $82.9 and the Strait of Hormuz blockade threatening global supply, the NOK is finding relative support despite its lack of G10 scorecard momentum. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; contrarian to 100% retail long positioning while below key SMAs. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 13 Aug — market bias Hold. Risk: A sudden de-escalation in the Persian Gulf lowers oil prices and triggers a retail-led USD/NOK short squeeze.
